transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Janelle Carter (PolarisHealth, Head of MLOps), Ben Ortiz (PolarisHealth, VP Eng), Maya Singh (PolarisHealth, Procurement)

Summary (auto): Renewal discussion focused on contract extension and capacity expansion into EU region. Discussed dedicated capacity, SLA, pricing tiers, and next steps for benchmarking and procurement.

00:00 Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, really appreciate it. um quick agenda   renewal timing, capacity upgrades (eu), and any compliance/contract items.
00:22 Janelle: thanks samira yeah we wanted to make sure we had alignment before budget sign-off, we've got a board review on 09/10 so would like to lock something by end of august if possible.
00:35 Ben: hi all, quick context   current usage is north america heavy, but product team launching EU feature H2 so we need region expansion and reserved capacity.
00:50 Diego: thanks, Ben. so just to confirm: you're looking at a dedicated pool in eu-west, plus continuation of hosted api in na?
01:05 Ben: correct. still want hosted in NA for dev, and dedicated in EU for production due to data residency.
01:14 Maya: procurement question   what are the typical lead times and contract length options? 12 or 24 months?
01:28 Samira: we usually offer 12 or 24; we can structure a 12-month renewal with optional extension, or a 24-month with better unit pricing. lead time for provisioning dedicated pool is usually 2-3 weeks once PO is in and capacity reserved, we can expedite with a deposit.
01:45 Janelle: okay that helps. curious about burst capacity and SLA   our SREs want 99.95 and fast failover to NA if eu has issues.
02:00 Diego: we support routing policies   can do primary eu with automatic fallback to na, but you'll see higher latency when falling back. for 99.95 we can add an SLA clause on dedicated tier, and configure cross-region fallback.
02:18 Janelle: latency numbers? P95?
02:22 Diego: from our internal benchmarks for similar customers eu-dedicated P95 is about 120-160ms for 1k concurrent rps with continuous batching; fallback to na adds ~80-150ms depending on route. i'll share the exact benchmark spreadsheet.
02:40 Ben: and cost delta between hosted and dedicated?
02:44 Samira: dedicated is committed monthly capacity; typically lower per-token at scale, but you pay reserved capacity. example: their current committed capacity cost could drop ~20-35% per token for steady load. i'll attach a worked example in the quote.
02:58 Ben: cool. also need to confirm encryption and audit logs for compliance   SOC 2 is a must.
03:05 Samira: yes we have SOC 2 Type II, we can share the report and the audit log retention options. for private key management we integrate with KMS/HSM in dedicated/private deployments.
03:18 Maya: do you support customer-managed keys in the hosted plan?
03:22 Diego: customer-managed keys require the private deployment or dedicated with KMS integration; hosted standard doesn't support CMK for now.
03:32 Maya: that's a blocker if we need CMK. i think for prod we'll need dedicated with KMS.
03:36 Janelle: agreed.
03:40 Samira: noted. next up   timeline and procurement steps?
03:45 Maya: procurement needs an itemized quote and order of operations: pricing, contract, SLAs, and an SOW for migration if needed.
03:55 Samira: we'll provide that. also want to flag model compatibility   are you planning to change models or keep same inference patterns?
04:02 Ben: mostly same models but hoping to increase throughput and add a reranker. might change token distributions a bit.
04:12 Diego: reranking and additional token context increases KV cache pressure; we'll size the dedicated pool with extra memory for KV and suggest quantization if you need more capacity.
04:24 Ben: okay. any concerns about throughput bumps from product launch? we expect a 2.5x increase in peak.
04:30 Diego: for 2.5x peak we recommend a burst pool and autoscale policy; there is also an option for reserving burst credits. we'll include configuration options in the quote.
04:45 Janelle: any competitors we should be aware of if we ask our infra team? they mentioned Bedrock and Anthropic when evaluating.
04:50 Samira: right, we sometimes see customers comparing unit economics vs Bedrock or Anthropic. our differentiator is the production-first controls and cost levers like batching/caching.
05:03 Ben: noted. procurement likely to push for multi-cloud pricing comparisons.
05:08 Maya: on contract length, 24 months with a mid-term review could be attractive if pricing is good.
05:15 Samira: we can do a 24-month with a 12-month checkpoint and a rollback clause for unreasonable regressions.
05:24 Janelle: ok good.
05:30 06:00 Diego: (technical) quick note about eu deployment: we can deploy in eu-west-1, and offer data residency   logs kept in-region, and option to redact or route telemetry to your audit account. one caveat: some GPUs have different perf on the eu hardware; i'll run a perf test on our eu cluster to get more accurate p95 numbers.
06:20 Ben: when can you run that?
06:24 Diego: i can start tests this week; will need expected traffic profile   small/large sequences, average tokens, concurrency.
06:34 Janelle: i'll send traffic patterns and current token distribution by EOD tomorrow.
06:40 Diego: perfect.
06:45 Samira: pricing   i'll do three scenarios: 12mo renewal, 24mo renewal, and 12mo with capacity add-on for eu only. include committed rps tiers and burst credits.
06:58 Maya: procurement needs to know if we can amortize onboarding costs.
07:02 Samira: yes we can spread onboarding and migration cost over the contract term; i'll show monthly amortized versions.
07:12 Ben: any reference customers using eu dedicated?
07:16 Samira: yes, i'll pull two references   health/saas customers with EU setups.
07:23 Janelle: great. we also need a security questionnaire   can you provide that?
07:28 Diego: we have a self-hosted security questionnaire and a standard infosec deck, i'll share both.
07:34 Samira: re: legal   do you have any required contract terms or must we use your template?
07:38 Maya: we typically prefer our PO and our DPA, but open to redlines.
07:43 Samira: we accept customer redlines; i'll loop our legal team once we get a redline pack.
07:50 Ben: timeline recap   board review 09/10; procurement needs final quote by end of August.
07:56 Samira: understood, we'll aim to get the pricing and perf results in the next week.
08:02 Diego: question from me   what's your P95 target for the new eu region?
08:06 Janelle: we'd like P95 < 200ms for production flows.
08:11 Diego: that should be achievable with dedicated and correct batching; i'll validate with tests.
08:16 Samira: any other blockers?
08:20 Maya: just the CMK requirement and procurement timeline; both covered.
08:24 Ben: also need demo of routing and failover for SRE; maybe a joint session with our infra team.
08:30 Diego: happy to run a technical deep dive and simulation   propose a 60m session next week.
08:36 Samira: i'll coordinate availability.
08:40 Janelle: sounds good.
08:44 Samira: okay i'm going to recap next steps   we'll send: 1) updated renewal quote with eu capacity options and pricing (Samira) 2) EU perf benchmark spreadsheet and logs (Diego) 3) SOC 2 & security questionnaire + reference customers (Samira/Diego) 4) proposed dates for infra deep dive (Samira).
09:02 Maya: and procurement needs the itemized quote to start PO.
09:06 Samira: noted. any last questions?
09:09 Ben: none from me.
09:11 Janelle: all good.
09:13 Samira: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and timelines.
09:18 Meeting end.
